judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed completion date subject to adjustments as provided in the Contract Documents; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the original 4.3's calendar-day count, and the commencement date it runs from is qualified by Addendum 4.1's 'pending approval of permits'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bonus of 'a sum to be determined' to be 'divided between the key management staff, as determined by the Owner' fixes neither amount nor method, and is close to an unenforceable agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 (changes in the Contract Sum only by Change Order), 8.1.1 (no compensation for off-site personnel) and Addendum 8.1.8 (management costs covered by the Fee).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Current best estimate', 'industry-standard figures', 'as agreed with Owner' and an Owner termination right 'in Owner's sole and absolute discretion' if the Preliminary Budget is not acceptable are all open-ended, and the clause never says what happens if bids exceed the estimate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The discretionary termination right stands beside Article 13 and A201 Article 14's enumerated termination grounds, and the fast-track Change Order pricing scheme competes with 5.2.6, 6.1 and 12.1.5's Guaranteed Maximum Price machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition' is a counterfactual test that will be argued about after any emergency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carries the same number as the Agreement's 7.7.2, which it narrows, and A201 10.6 permits emergency action at the Contractor's discretion with compensation under Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a proviso about the absence of collectible insurance being due to the Contractor's failure to maintain insurance; wordy but reasonably definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and modifies the Agreement's 7.7.3 and interacts with 8.1.6, Article 16's blank insurance limits and A201 11.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of items the Fee 'shall cover' ending with the sweeping statement that 'none of these items shall be subject to direct reimbursement under Article 7' — the reach of the list against Article 7's specifics is exactly a general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7 expressly reimburses several of the same categories (7.5.4 telephone, postage, facsimiles; 7.6.6 data processing; 7.2.2-7.2.3 administrative personnel), and it also reuses the number of the original 8.1.8 on the Guaranteed Maximum Price.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear notice-and-opportunity condition before the Contractor may take discounts for itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Builds on Paragraph 9.1's allocation rule, which it expressly references; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' makes payment documentation subject to an unmeasured satisfaction standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reuses the number 12.1.4 already occupied by the Agreement's substantiation provision, so both must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed but definite list of what the subcontractor statement must show.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 11 accounting records and A201 9.3.1; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires executed lien waivers 'establishing payment or satisfaction' of amounts included in the very application for which payment has not yet been made — a timing paradox on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.3.3 and 9.10.2 set out the ordinary sequence of title warranty and final releases, and Addendum 12.2.2 keys final payment to a lien-free title endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require' is a catch-all appended to two enumerated specifics, with only 'reasonably' to bound it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the Agreement 12.1.4's 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect' and A201 9.3.1's 'such data substantiating the Contractor's right to payment'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes retainage at five percent and repeats the alternative fee computations without saying which applies to a lump-sum fee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the 'N/A' retainage in the Agreement's 12.1.7.3 and sits beside 12.1.8's not-less-than-ten-percent subcontractor retainage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single added condition to final payment, clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a third condition to 12.2.1 and drives the fifty-day clock in Addendum 12.2.2, but nothing in the Agreement obliges anyone to record the Notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative triggers joined by 'whichever is earlier', one of which (a lien-free title endorsement) depends on third-party action.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the Agreement's 12.2.2 thirty-day rule and must be reconciled with 12.2.3's seven-day final certificate timetable and A201 9.10.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' leaves it open whether any one of them may bind the Owner alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 names Mary Williamson as the authorized representative but allows action by Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson, a third formulation of the same office.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A survival and materiality lead-in to the warranties; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 1.5.2, 3.2.1 and 13.4.1 on cumulative remedies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A solvency warranty covering both the Contractor and unnamed Subcontractors, which the Contractor cannot fully know; the subparagraph is also mislabelled '(3)' for '(a)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 2.2.1 imposes the mirror-image financial-evidence duty on the Owner; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficient experience and competence' is a soft warranty standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise to furnish tools and equipment sits awkwardly with Article 7 and Exhibits A and C, which let the Contractor charge for the same tools and equipment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A licensing warranty in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.7.1-3.7.2 compliance duties; no internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A site-visit and familiarity representation in standard form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates A201 1.5.2 and 3.2.1 and must be read with A201 4.3.4's relief for concealed or unknown conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Agreement as modified by the First Addendum; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with the Addendum's incorporation recital; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the 1997 A201 as modified by the Supplementary Conditions; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the Agreement's 15.1.2, which calls the General Conditions 'the 1991 edition', so the two enumerations disagree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward incorporation of A201 Articles 1 through 14.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 of the Agreement gives the Agreement precedence over inconsistent documents, so the incorporation is not unqualified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence says that when a paragraph 'is modified or deleted by these Supplementary Conditions, the unaltered provision of the General Conditions shall remain in effect' — as written it preserves the very provision it says is deleted, a mechanical defect that inverts the intended meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs every clash between the Supplementary Conditions and A201 (for example the two versions of 2.4.1 at c131 and c168), so the error propagates through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It converts every Architect approval into an Owner approval while denying the Owner any responsibility 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner', a broad disclaimer against an equally broad grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.2.1-4.2.13 vest interpretive and certifying authority in the Architect and A201 4.2.2/4.2.3 disclaim Owner control, so the reallocation of consent rights has to be harmonised across Article 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Better quality or greater quantity' and 'more stringent requirement', resolved 'in accordance with the Architect's interpretation as approved by the Owner', is a one-sided conflict rule whose application is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 says that where the other Contract Documents are inconsistent with the Agreement, the Agreement governs — a different and potentially opposite resolution rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional precedence rule for dimensions and drawing scales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 1.2.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No extra charge or compensation will be allowed on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated on the Drawings' is absolute, yet the same paragraph tells the Contractor to submit differences for resolution before proceeding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.2.1-3.2.3 say the Contractor's review is not for the purpose of discovering errors and that it is not liable for Document errors it did not recognise, and A201 4.3.4 allows equitable adjustment for differing conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently detailed drawings' and 'minor change ... due to actual field conditions' are undefined thresholds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.4.1 gives the Architect authority to order minor changes by written order, a different route for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause names one authorized representative (Mary Williamson) and then permits binding action by three different people, an internal inconsistency in two consecutive sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 14.3 and Addendum 14.3 [Revised] give still different lists, and 14.5 requires ten days' notice to change a representative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single seven-day cure period followed by Owner self-help, clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 2.4.1 (reproduced at c168) requires a second seven-day notice before the Owner may act; the two versions of the same numbered paragraph flatly differ, and Supplementary Condition c124's savings sentence muddies which survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'detailed timetable of all activities and events' that is 'deemed attached to Document A111 as a part of the Contract Documents' as it is developed — a document that becomes binding without execution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 and 15.1 enumerate the Contract Documents exhaustively and A201 1.1.2 says the Contract may be amended only by Modification, so unilaterally developed schedules becoming Contract Documents is hard to square.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Phase-based revisions with cost estimates that 'shall become part of the Contract Documents'; the effect of an estimate becoming a Contract Document is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 says the Contract Sum may change only by Change Order, and Addendum 6.5 has its own Preliminary Budget procedure, so three provisions govern the same pricing evolution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A shop-drawing approval and competence warranty; 'if required by the Architect or the Owner or applicable law' is a clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.12.10 says the Contractor is not required to provide professional design services unless specified, which this clause partly cuts across.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed pleading requirements for time claims; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplements A201 4.3.7.1-4.3.7.2 consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled ('for each aie of the number of causes of delay') and the concurrent-delay rule it states cannot be read with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 8.3.1 grants extensions for delays beyond the Contractor's control without a concurrency rule, so the two must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars claims based on course of conduct, implied acceptance and unjust enrichment 'whether or not there is, in fact, any unjust enrichment', a sweeping one-sided bar whose reach over extra work performed at the Owner's direction is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.3 (Construction Change Directives), 7.4 (minor changes by written order), 4.3.4 (concealed conditions) and Addendum 6.5's evolving pricing all allow adjustments without a signed Change Order.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final settlement of all matters relating to the change ... including all direct and indirect costs' is a broad accord whose reach over later impact and delay claims is a familiar battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.3.7 and 7.3.8-7.3.9 contemplate later adjustments and interim determinations, which this finality rule curtails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In their sole discretion' joint-check right with express disclaimers of privity; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.6.2 requires the Contractor to pay Subcontractors out of amounts received, and 9.6.4 disclaims any Owner obligation to Subcontractors, which this dovetails with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions the final Certificate on all warranties being 'received and accepted by the Owner', with acceptance unqualified by any reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.10.1 requires the Architect to issue the final Certificate promptly on completion and Agreement 12.2.3 sets a seven-day deadline, so an open-ended Owner acceptance condition sits uneasily with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear exclusion of tools and construction equipment from the Owner's property insurance, with a waiver-of-subrogation requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 11.4.1 requires all-risk insurance on the Work including materials, and 11.4.7's waiver of subrogation extends to property insurance 'applicable to the Work', so the boundary of covered property matters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All reasonable costs (including attorneys' fees and court and settlement expenses) properly attributable thereto' is a fee-shifting formula with an elastic attribution test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates A201 11.4.1.2's remedy for the Owner's failure to insure and interacts with A201 4.3.10's waiver of consequential damages and Article 16's blank insurance limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exhibit says hand-tool cost 'shall be borne by the Contractor' and in the very next sentence adds a flat 5% of payroll to cover those same tools; the illustrative list ('include, but are not limited to ... air compressors ... beam saws ... etc.') also stretches 'hand tools' well beyond its ordinary sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.1 reimburses only tools 'fully consumed' with salvage credits, 8.1.5 excludes rental costs of machinery except under 7.5.2, and 8.1.7 excludes any cost not expressly described in Article 7 — none of which authorises a percentage markup.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes the general liability premium 'at the rate of 1% of the total labor and subcontractors' costs' — a formula that bears no necessary relation to premium actually paid, and 'labor and subcontractors' costs' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.1 reimburses only 'that portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract', and 8.1.7 bars costs not expressly described in Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'Subcontract' costs, then extends the definition to unnamed 'certain vendors' costs ... including; rubbish hauling and tipping fees, engineering and consulting fees, temporary facilities fees, freight charges, etc.' — an enumerated list closed with 'etc.' whose reach cannot be fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.2 reimburses taxes 'imposed by a governmental authority that are related to the Work' without this exclusion scheme, and 8.1.7 limits costs to Article 7 items.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional list of Contract Documents and Modifications; conventional and closed-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 gives itself precedence and 15.1 leaves the Drawings and Specifications unenumerated, so the definition operates on an incomplete set.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entire-agreement and no-privity provisions in standard form; 'may be amended or modified only by Modification' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 reinforces it, but Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 let schedules and cost estimates become Contract Documents without a Modification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Work' is defined broadly to include 'all other labor, materials, equipment and services provided or to be provided by the Contractor to fulfill the Contractor's obligations'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The scope defining documents (Drawings and Specifications) are not enumerated in 15.1.4-15.1.5, which leaves this definition without a fixed referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition of the Project; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 6.1 on separate contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Drawings; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.5 of the Agreement lists no Drawings, so what qualifies is left to extrinsic proof.
